milestone: WP-01 strict native filename transport and Win32 convention diagnostics (partial WP-01)
configuration: Release C++20 strict warnings; installed ckVision SDK; Windows static CRT
sanitizer_scope: 7 translation units: native names, strict scalar codec, name mapping, Win32 name diagnostics, prior native-name tests, new mapping tests, ckVision test host. 20 cases including exhaustive Unicode scalar coverage. All 23 Files CTest suites separately passed on all hosts.

unicode_scalar_coverage.checks: UTF8/UTF16 encode/decode round trips for every scalar; independent boundary byte/unit vectors; malformed, truncated, overlong, surrogate, out-of-range encodings; zero/noncharacters; prior injective display cases

qualified_behaviors: Same-encoding native components retain original bytes/units, including invalid UTF8 and unpaired UTF16. Cross encoding uses strict scalar UTF8/UTF16 with no replacement, normalization, case folding, locale conversion or BOM removal.

Unrepresentable encoding/component boundaries yield Unsupported without a prefix. Invalid configuration/source/destination tags yield Failed. Input/output native-storage byte budget exhaustion yields Unknown without a prefix.
Shared scalar codecs serve existing escaped display and strict transport; display strings are never parsed as operation names.

NativeName::is_valid shares factory boundary predicates; moved-from invalid components are refused before native lookup, held-child observation, pane publication or mapping. Validity is independent of Unicode encoding validity.

Fixed-size Win32 diagnostics report empty/navigation components, forbidden characters including stream syntax and controls, device-alias risk including superscript digits, and trailing-dot/space rewrite risk. Shared device-risk recognition also serves the Windows absolute-path inspection guard.
Generic Win32 convention matches and successful transport grant no destination acceptance, collision freedom, path/length validity or creation authority.

native_qualification.macos: APFS; mapped BMP/astral Unicode names; raw backslash/newline components; ordinary POSIX colon filename; literal CON/trailing-dot names remain identifiable. Invalid-UTF8 filename creation is not asserted on APFS.
native_qualification.linux: Lima ckdev Debian 13 arm64/ext4; same mapped Unicode/literal/colon fixtures plus actual invalid-UTF8 byte 0xFF in a component with backslash/newline.
native_qualification.windows: V: ReFS; mapped Unicode names and raw unpaired UTF16 component; metadata file lookup rejects colon stream syntax; private extended-path CON and trailing-dot files queried through counted-relative NT names and explicitly removed through literal paths.

limitations: Native filename transport is not an operation capability or a destination namespace comparison. Full case/normalization/alias/short-name collision handling, destination filesystem restrictions and per-API path/component limits remain required.
NameMappingLimits is a resource budget (default 64KiB, hard 1MiB for each input/output native representation), not the filesystem reported or enforceable name limit.

POSIX cross-encoding output is explicitly UTF8 bytes; there is no automatic locale, WTF8, surrogate escape or substitution fallback. Unrepresentable cases require an explicit higher-layer decision, never an automatic rename.
Win32 diagnostics are generic compatibility risks, not universal filesystem rejection. Literal counted NT names may be valid even when Win32 conventions flag them.

No Files GUI or mutation engine exists. Remaining native inventories/provider coordination, operation-specific capabilities, full filesystem/time fakes and page-backed listing work are incomplete WP-01 requirements.

native_spelling_readback.checks: Fresh bounded native enumeration must reach End and contain the exact expected native byte/UTF16 component, independent of successful name lookup. No escaped display comparison.
native_spelling_readback.qualified: Mapped Unicode, unusual raw components, POSIX colon filenames and literal CON/trailing-dot fixture names on the corresponding native platforms.
